title: Localization preserves actual closed restriction on one module
statement: Fix a prime ell and commutative condensed rings R,K on profinite sets [sk-def-localizing-closure], and a ring-object map a:R -> K. Pull them back to every small pro-etale site [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Assume scalar extension along a_V preserves finite limits for every scheme V, and the regular K_V-module, restricted to R_V, is the colimit of R_V --ell--> R_V --ell--> ... with zeroth leg a_V. This is the defined predicate IsEllLocalizationCoefficient, with its cocone and specified zeroth leg. For a closed immersion t:T0 -> T of qcqs schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and any R_T-module H, if the actual ordinary module-derived restriction rho_R,t on H[0] is an isomorphism, then rho_K,t on (K_T tensor_R_T H)[0] is an isomorphism. The maps rho are the adjunction-unit-derived restriction maps [def-sfb-closed-restriction-actual-map]. No finite-model, lattice, torsion-rigidity, or complement hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the specified regular-module telescope, tensor it with H, and apply the tensor adjunction and colimit preservation. The zeroth leg is the coefficient map, so restriction of K tensor_R H is the ell-telescope of H with its actual R-action. Cartesian pullback identifies its pullback with the ell-telescope of t^*H.

Apply bounded-below filtered section continuity on both qcqs schemes to the degree-zero telescopes. Naturality at each leg identifies the restriction on the colimit with the colimit of the restriction on H in every cohomological degree. Each such map is invertible by hH. The closed-restriction derived-operations theorem supplies the normalized simultaneous filtered representatives of the actual restriction.

Finite-limit preservation of extension makes coefficient restriction preserve K-injectives. A K-injective resolution over K therefore computes sections after restriction to R. Choose a second K-injective resolution on T0 after pullback. Coefficient forgetting preserves the adjunction-unit section map and the augmentation-compatible chain comparison. Scalar coherence, Cartesian coefficients and the two-resolution formula identify the map obtained above with the actual K-derived restriction. All cohomology maps are invertible, hence the derived restriction is invertible.
